subject.title: feat(codex): config to disable or scope the native hook relay (#91009)

question: Should the Codex plugin expose operator-controlled `nativeHookRelay.enabled` and event scoping when those settings can suppress native-hook behavior used for approvals, policies, or loop detection?
rationale: The branch is intentionally additive and opt-in, but the acceptable safety semantics and the relationship to the other open relay proposals are product and policy choices rather than a mechanical implementation detail.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow opt-in contract
options.body: Define which events remain mandatory under active approval or trusted-policy conditions, consolidate the setting shape, and require live proof before merge.

options.title: Limit the change to default relay reductions
options.body: Prioritize the existing idle-`PreToolUse` reduction and defer an operator disable/scope surface until a broader relay policy is agreed.

options.title: Choose a different consolidated policy proposal
options.body: Adopt a single alternative relay-policy design and close or rework overlapping proposals to prevent competing configuration contracts.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Define which events remain mandatory under active approval or trusted-policy conditions, consolidate the setting shape, and require live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their adjacent active PR is the closest available implementation history for the relay event-selection boundary, although ownership confidence is limited without a completed current-main history trace.
